question.text: Consider separate solutions of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mi>OH</mi><mo> </mo><mfenced><mi>aq</mi></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><msub><mi>Mg</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mfenced><msub><mi>PO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msub><mo> </mo><mfenced><mi>aq</mi></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>250</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><mi>KBr</mi><mo> </mo><mfenced><mi>aq</mi></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>125</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><msub><mi>Na</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>PO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo> </mo><mfenced><mi>aq</mi></mfenced></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. Which statement is true about these solutions, assuming all salts to be strong electrolytes?

options.text: They all have the same osmotic pressure.

solution.text:
Osmotic pressure  π=iCRT(i is  Van't  Hoff factor, C is concentration)

π=iC at same temperature.

C2H5OH=1x0.5=0.5Mg3(PO4)2=5x0.1=0.5KBr=2x0.25=0.5Na3PO4=4x0.125=0.5

The solutions are isotonic as they have the same osmotic pressure.
